summary: Our project addresses the issue of spacecraft and machines that embarked on space missions and remain stranded out there. Our team developed a solution through an interactive website featuring an educational storytelling format for children and youth. It narrates a simple animated story about an alien named Topi and a girl named Sofia. The story begins with Topi crash-landing on Earth, escaping from hostile creatures that invaded his home planet. Events unfold until Sofia's curiosity leads her to ask Topi to take her with him into space to explore it together. On their journey to his kingdom, they notice various machines scattered across deep space, prompting Sofia to ask about each machine and its mission, while Topi answers all her questions. The project aims to target school children and young minds, feeding the imaginations of space enthusiasts and science lovers. We hope our project inspires you and benefits the target audience
details:
AFTER ORBIT: An Interactive Journey Through Space Exploration

AFTER ORBIT is an interactive educational website designed to make the history of space exploration more engaging, accessible, and enjoyable, especially for young learners.

1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

The website takes users on a journey through NASA's space exploration history, focusing on the spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific technologies that helped humans explore the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

Instead of presenting information as ordinary articles, AFTER ORBIT organizes it into interactive chapters. Each chapter introduces a space mission or technology through scientific facts, storytelling, and conversations between two characters, Topi and Sofia.

Users can explore a 3D space scene, browse the archive, search and filter chapters, listen to character narration, and learn through interactive educational activities and quizzes. The project also introduces ORI, an AI companion concept intended to help users understand scientific information and navigate the archive.

2. What are the benefits of the project?

  • Makes complex space science easier to understand through simple explanations and storytelling.
  • Encourages curiosity about astronomy, engineering, robotics, and scientific discovery.
  • Combines education with interactive experiences instead of relying only on traditional reading.
  • Helps young learners remember scientific information through characters, visual elements, and quizzes.
  • Provides an accessible starting point for students who are interested in space but do not know where to begin.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make space exploration feel closer to students and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, programmers, and explorers.

We want users to move beyond simply memorizing the names of space missions. We want them to understand the challenges behind these missions, appreciate the technology that made them possible, and become curious enough to explore scientific topics independently.

In the long term, we hope AFTER ORBIT can grow into an engaging educational platform that connects space science with technology, creativity, and critical thinking.

4. What tools, programming languages, and software did we use?

The project was developed using web technologies and interactive development tools, including:

  • React: Building the interactive user interface and reusable components.
  • TypeScript: Organizing the code and improving reliability.
  • HTML and CSS: Structuring and styling the website.
  • JavaScript: Implementing interactive features and functionality.
  • Vite: Development environment and build tool.
  • Framer Motion: Creating animations and smooth transitions.
  • Lucide React: Providing interface icons.
  • React Router: Managing navigation between pages.
  • Visual Studio Code: Writing and managing the code.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control and collaboration.

The project is primarily software-based and does not require custom physical hardware.

5. How is the project creative?

Our main creative idea is to turn space exploration into a story-driven experience.

We introduced Topi, a fictional cosmic prince who arrives on Earth, and Sofia, his curious human friend. Together, they guide users through real NASA missions and technologies. This gives scientific information a narrative context without losing its educational purpose.
